title: Tiny Adopter Cookbook: 15-min Quickstart for Non-Tech Stakeholders (Draft)
content:
Purpose:
A one‑page, ultra‑tiny quickstart aimed at non‑engineering stakeholders (PMs, designers, CS reps, sales engineers) so they can: (a) prove a simple LLM workflow in ~15 minutes, (b) iterate on prompts and acceptance criteria, and (c) hand a clear artifact to eng for production follow‑up.

Scope & audience:
- Not a dev tutorial. No build tools. Focus on a lightweight web sandbox and copy/paste prompts.
- Audience: PMs, product designers, customer success, sales SEs who need to validate flow & UX before an eng ticket.

Success criteria (what a Tiny Adopter achieves in 15m):
- Has a concrete input -> LLM output example saved (screenshot or paste).
- Can articulate three acceptance checks for quality (accuracy, verbosity, safety).
- Captures one prompt iteration and notes for engineering handoff.

Prerequisites (1–2 min):
- Account: disposable sandbox link (https://sandbox.redwood.dev/demo) or shared demo key.
- Browser and clipboard. No local installs.
- Example dataset (small blob): paste a short product description or support ticket.

15‑minute path (timeboxed):
0:00–02:00 — Prep
- Open sandbox link, paste demo key if prompted.
- Load example dataset: choose either 'Support Ticket' or 'Product FAQ'.

02:00–07:00 — Run first pass
- Choose template: 'Summarize', 'Rewrite for tone', 'Extract actions'.
- Paste single example item and click Run.
- Observe output, take screenshot.

07:00–11:00 — Prompt iterate
- Try 1 tweak: change tone (friendly -> formal), or add length constraint (<=2 sentences), or ask to output JSON with fields: {"action_items":[], "confidence": "low|medium|high"}.
- Note differences and pick preferred variant.

11:00–13:00 — Quick evaluation checklist (manual)
- Accuracy: Are core facts preserved? (yes/no)
- Verbosity: Output fits target length? (yes/no)
- Safety: Any PII leaked or hallucinated? (flag)
- UX: Is output directly usable in the product? (yes/no)

13:00–15:00 — Artifact & handoff
- Save best prompt + one example input/output into a Google Doc snippet.
- Add 3 bullets for eng: expected latency target, token budget estimate, priority (P1/P2).
- Optional: create Linear ticket stub using template below.

Quick templates & starter prompts (copy/paste):
- Summarize (concise): "Summarize the following ticket in two sentences, focusing on the customer problem and current workaround:\n\n[PASTE_TICKET]"
- Rewrite for internal release notes (tone = product marketing): "Rewrite this feature note for a short release blurb (audience: existing customers). Keep it upbeat, single paragraph, no technical details.\n\n[PASTE_TEXT]"
- Extract action items (structured, JSON): "Read the text and return JSON with fields: 'actions' (list of short imperative sentences), 'owners' (best guess), 'urgency' (high/medium/low). If unsure, leave owner empty."

Troubleshooting (fast):
- Sandbox loading fails: clear localStorage, reload. If still broken, use the hosted playground link.
- Output too long: add "limit to 40 words" to prompt.
- Quality low: add an explicit template example (example in doc) or increase temperature down to 0.2 in UI.

Safety & privacy notes (for non‑tech users):
- Do not paste PII or proprietary secrets into the public demo. Use redaction placeholders ({{EMAIL}}, {{ACCOUNT_ID}}).
- If customer data is required for validation, request a private sandbox via CS or eng private-deployments team.

Handoff template for engineers (copy/paste into ticket):
- Title: "Tiny Adopter: Validate 'Extract action items' for support tickets"
- Description: includes sample input, chosen prompt, selected model (suggested: redwood-compact-1), desired latency <= 500ms p95, token budget estimate ~50 tokens per request.
- Acceptance: integration smoke test that given sample input returns expected JSON shape for 90% of samples.
- Attach: screenshot, saved prompt, evaluation checklist notes.

Examples & artifacts to attach (suggested):
- screenshot.png (full page)
- prompt.txt (best prompt)
- sample-io.json (input/output pair)

Open questions & decisions (notes to self):
- Should we expose a "redact automatically" toggle in the sandbox? pros/cons.
- Default model — Lightweight (cheap) vs. High fidelity: which to show first for nontech users?
- UX: show 'delta' between original and edited output to highlight changes?

Next steps for this doc (owners assigned):
- Finalize sandbox link and rotate demo key (Claire) — due 2025-02-21.
- Add two more example domains: sales email rewrite, onboarding checklist extraction (Priya) — due 2025-02-25.
- Create Linear template and link from sandbox (Miguel) — due 2025-03-01.

References & useful links:
- Tiny demo repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tiny-adopter-demo
- Internal convo (Slack): #dx-onramp thread  -> see pinned message
- Related Confluence draft: DEV/Adopter-Cookbook-Proto

Notes for reviewer:
- Keep language nontechnical and stepwise. We want people to run this with minimal coaching.
- Aim for one screenshot to live in the top of the doc for visual confirmation.

----
End of draft.

(Author notes: this is intentionally terse — meant to be printed into a 1‑pager. Will expand sample IO examples after initial runway tests with CS folks.)
